sections.overview: Lethrinus reticulatus Valenciennes, 1830 is a marine emperor fish in the family Lethrinidae.
sections.identification: It has an olive-grey to tan body with irregular dark blotches and reddish markings on the snout and around the pectoral-fin base; it reaches about 40 centimetres total length.
sections.habitat: This tropical Indo-West Pacific fish is associated with reefs and nearby soft bottoms, generally at about 5–30 metres depth.
sections.diet: Its diet is poorly documented; accounts suggest it takes benthic invertebrates and small fish.
sections.behavior: It is reported alone or in groups, but detailed species-specific behavioural observations are scarce.
sections.reproduction: The consulted sources provide little information on its reproductive biology.
sections.ecology: It shares the genus Lethrinus with the orange-striped emperor (L. obsoletus) and drab emperor (L. ravus), described in the companion profiles for comparison.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment dated 2015 classified it as Least Concern.
